A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MIPLIB-NL benchmark and construction pipeline. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–J are available for comparison, including content relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 14 systems, including Pass@1, Pass@8, execution failures, scale-dependent performance, and error case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a structural-complexity audit, detailed error distributions, construction-validation counts, and a held-out fine-tuning experiment.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain expert structural abstraction, scaffold-based NL generation, optional linguistic polishing, and reconstruction/expert validation. Added explanations clarify this pipeline; the supplementary LoRA experiment does not revise the proposed construction method.

E1.justification: The documented evaluation suite retains MIPLIB-NL and the same ten prior benchmarks; the LoRA experiment repartitions existing instances. Appendix I newly mentions early nonlinear and multi-objective trials, but provides insufficient information about tested instances or evaluations to establish whether actual task coverage expanded.

E2.justification: The original 14-system comparisons are unchanged. New Table 10 compares Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct before and after LoRA fine-tuning with GPT-5.1 and a Union reference aggregating available frontier-model runs.

E3.justification: Table 10 introduces a 179-training/44-test split with zero family overlap. New analyses introduce an L0–L3 structural-complexity rubric and relative scale grouping for error subtypes. The existing Pass@1/Pass@8 protocol, temperature, and objective-value tolerance remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends the supplementary analysis beyond v1's coarse error categories and examples. Figure 8 audits structure preserved in benchmark descriptions; Figures 18–19 compare detailed error subtypes across benchmarks and scale groups; Table 10 tests whether in-domain fine-tuning helps a smaller model.

E5.justification: Figure 18 newly reports Holm-adjusted p-values for pairwise error-distribution comparisons, and Appendix G asserts significant subtype shifts across scale groups. v1 contains no corresponding significance tests. Existing eight-attempt sampling and seed information are retained.

E6.justification: The original Pass@1, Pass@8, and execution-error tables are numerically unchanged, but substantial supplementary results are added. Figure 8 reports 92.1% L0 and 4.1% L2+L3 descriptions; Section 3.4 reports 163 primary-validation successes and 60 secondary-stage retentions from 245 candidates. New Table 10 reports Base-7B versus LoRA-7B executability of 1/44 versus 14/44 and correctness of 0/44 versus 5/44. Figures 18–19 add detailed error distributions.

T1.justification: The problem mappings, information-theoretic compression discussion in Appendix C, and mathematical scaffold definitions in Appendix D are retained. The new empirical categorization and explanatory paragraphs introduce no substantive mathematical derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's four contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: faithful reconstruction of 223 MIPLIB instances and exposure of industrial-scale modeling failures. The supplementary additions do not redefine these principal contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning fine-tuning benefits versus the remaining frontier-model gap, subtype-specific modeling bottlenecks, and verification as the main obstacle to scaling construction. It also explicitly acknowledges structured prior benchmarks and discusses possible extensions beyond MILP in Appendix I.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 more explicitly documents re-expanding scaffolds for algebraic equivalence checking, while Appendix G identifies prompts, generated code, execution outcomes, and traces as diagnostic inputs. The LoRA checkpoint and adaptation are identified, but training hyperparameters remain unspecified. Existing schemas, prompts, hardware information, and access instructions are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations and discussion concerning OptArgus, MM-OptBench, OptiTrust, Step-Opt, and error-driven modeling, and replaces the ApIO reference with Bi et al. Appendix A more explicitly distinguishes MIPLIB-NL from prior benchmarks that already preserve some loop structure.

P1.justification: Most prose and the section hierarchy remain intact. v2 adds localized explanations and analytical paragraphs, acknowledgments, and an impact statement, and updates author ordering, equal-contribution attribution, and publication text.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 8, 18, and 19 and Table 10, relocates the former Table 9 as Table 4, and reflows existing displays. Figure 1's caption now explains the median annotations. Existing figures and tables largely retain their designs and content.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful validation accounting, a structural audit, and held-out training evidence while preserving the original benchmark results. However, its new diagnostic figures have an unexplained mismatch: Figure 18 assigns 66.0% of MIPLIB-NL modeling errors to data/index coupling, whereas every stated within-MIPLIB-NL bucket in Figure 19 reports only 8.3–11.0%. Without an explanation of differing populations or aggregation, this undermines the added analysis and prevents a reliable net quality judgment.
